sources.citation: C. Hart Merriam papers relating to work with California Indians (Bancroft Library, BANC FILM 1556), reel 111 (ethnosynonymy cards), reel 33 'Vocabularies' (= Golla Appendix A G/6d/V22, 'O-kwahn-noo-choo-hish', Lottie O'Neal and Rose Ryan, Squaw Creek & Upper McCloud, 1925), reel 53 'Natural History Word Lists'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Reel 111 cards 'Okwanuchu' (copied from Handbook of American Indians pt.2 p.117, 1910: language 'in part close to that of the Shasta proper, but it contains a number of totally distinct words') and 'Oo-kwah-noo-tsoo' (Wintoon informant 1928). Reel 33 holds the handwritten 1925 vocabulary schedule but its scanned is unusable (no hit for 'kwahn'); it is a word list and cannot contain a stress statement. Reel 53 scanned has no Okwanuchu hit.

sources.citation: Survey of California and Other Indian Languages / California Language Archive. 'Okwanuchu' language page and CLA item list (langid 254).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Our only information about this language comes from fewer than 100 words recorded early in the 20th century.' CLA holds no archival items for Okwanuchu; further reading = Golla 2011 only.

sources.citation: Bright, William & D. L. Olmsted. 1959. A Shasta vocabulary. Kroeber Anthropological Society Papers 20: 1-55.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Shasta proper (shas1239), not Okwanuchu: phoneme inventory lists 'High pitch accent' for Shasta; Okwanuchu appears only as a group name ('okwanuchu K280, okwanuchu Cu, okwanutsu M'). Nothing on Okwanuchu stress.

sources.citation: Kroeber, A. L. 1925. Handbook of the Indians of California (BAE Bulletin 78), 'Shastan groups' pp. 279-284; 'The Okwanuchu' p. 284.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.284: 'The dialect is peculiar. Many words are practically pure Shasta; others are distorted to the very verge of recognizability, or utterly different.' Ethnographic; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Merriam, C. Hart. 1925. Vocabulary of O-kwahn-noo-choo-hish (Okwanuchu), Squaw Creek & Upper McCloud River, from Lottie O'Neal and Rose Ryan. Bancroft Library, C. Hart Merriam papers, BANC FILM 1556 reel 33 (Golla Appendix A: G/6d/V22).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The largest body of Okwanuchu data (c. 75 words, Merriam's orthography marks stressed syllables with an acute); the only place stress placement could be inferred from data. Handwritten schedule; scanned useless, 144 MB PDF not downloaded.

sources.citation: Dixon, Roland B. 1905. The Shasta-Achomawi: a new linguistic stock, with four new dialects. American Anthropologist n.s. 7(2): 213-217.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only published primary Okwanuchu data: seven words in the comparative table pp.216 (in'nux 'head', is'sawak 'ear', axta' 'blood', at'sa 'water', itu'ri 'salmon'..) carrying accent marks after the stressed syllable, plus p.215 'the general phonetic character of the Okwa'nuchu differs quite a little in some points from the Shasta, particularly in its fondness for nasals'. No statement about stress.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog lists a single reference (Golla 2011, a wordlist or less). Wikipedia cites Golla 2011:90-91, Du Bois 1935 (a few Waymaq words, e.g. atsa 'water') and Curtin 1884 ('Wailaki on McCloud', 18 words). No phonological description exists.
